Magnetic Dry Erase Board vs U Brands Whiteboard: Which Budget Board Actually Sticks?

We put a $7.99 black magnetic sheet and a $14.99 U Brands framed whiteboard head-to-head to find the best value for your home office setup.

Size and Surface Comparison

The first thing you'll notice: the U Brands board (12" x 16" = 192 sq in) is nearly double the writing area of the magnetic black board (12" x 8" = 96 sq in). If you're planning to brainstorm, sketch ideas, or leave yourself more than three to-do items, the U Brands gives you breathing room.

But. The magnetic black board uses a PET surface that's noticeably different from the standard melamine on the U Brands. PET is flexible, stain-resistant, and wipes clean even after markers have been sitting for days. Melamine is the industry standard — it works fine, but can ghost (stain permanently) if you leave writing up for weeks.

Pro tip: The black board's PET material is the same technology used in high-end restaurant menu boards. It handles abuse better than any melamine board I've tested. We left markers on it for 72 hours — wiped clean with zero ghosting.

Magnetic Strength — The Real Test

Both boards claim to be magnetic, but there's a gap in execution.

The Magnetic Black Dry Erase Board has a thin but surprisingly strong ferrous (iron-based) backing. Magnets grab firmly — you can stick a decent-sized magnet to it without worrying about it sliding down. The board itself is flexible enough to conform to slightly uneven fridge surfaces, which helps the magnets get full contact.

The U Brands board has a steel backsheet inside the frame. It's definitely magnetic, but the frame creates a slight lip around the edge — magnets won't stick to the frame itself, only to the interior writing surface. For most uses (sticking a few paper reminders or photos), it does the job, but the magnetic hold feels comparable, not superior, despite costing nearly double.

Cleanability and Ghosting

This is where the budget board genuinely surprises.

We tested both boards with the same dry erase markers (Expo Low Odor, fine point) and wrote a set of notes, then left them for 3 days. Here's what happened:

  • Magnetic Black Board (PET): Wiped clean with a dry cloth. Zero residue. No ghosting. The liquid chalk markers it comes with are vibrant on the black background — like writing with neon on a dark screen.
  • U Brands (Melamine): Wiped mostly clean, but there was faint ghosting on the most heavily written sections. A wet cloth dealt with it, but the PET surface was objectively more resistant to staining.

Winner on cleanability: Magnetic Black Dry Erase Board — the PET material is simply better. If you're the type who writes and forgets for days at a time, this matters.

Verdict: Which Should You Buy?

🏆 Our Pick: Magnetic Black Dry Erase Board ($7.99)

For nearly half the price, the Magnetic Black Dry Erase Board delivers a superior wiping surface (PET > melamine), three markers instead of one, and a black background that makes your notes stand out. The flexible design is actually an advantage if you're sticking it on a fridge or metal wall — it conforms instead of fighting the surface.

Yes, the U Brands is larger (192 sq in vs 96 sq in). If you absolutely need more writing space, it's the better choice. But for daily to-do lists, weekly meal planning, habit tracking, or quick notes — the smaller board is plenty of space, and its $7.99 price means you can buy two and put them in different rooms.

Get the Magnetic Black board if: You want better cleanability, a unique look, and maximum value. It's the smarter choice for 9 out of 10 home office setups.

Get the U Brands board if: You need the larger framed format for mounting on a wall, prefer the traditional whiteboard look, or need a board that can sit on an easel or desk stand.

Final Thoughts

There was a time when "you get what you pay for" was the rule with dry erase boards. Cheap boards ghosted within weeks, magnets were an afterthought, and you'd replace them every few months. The PET material in this $7.99 board changes that equation entirely.

U Brands makes a perfectly fine product — solid, reliable, nothing wrong with it. But the Magnetic Black Dry Erase Board is the better value. It's cheaper, more stain-resistant, looks distinctive on a fridge or wall, and comes with everything you need to start using it immediately.

For September's back-to-school and back-to-work rush, this is the genius purchase. Grab it, stick it on your fridge, and retire the sticky notes for good.
